articles.author: Mike Petriello
articles.title: Is Randy Arozarena or Seiya Suzuki a better free agent?
articles.take: Petriello shows Suzuki and Arozarena with identical four-year lines and leans Suzuki on bat speed, chase rate and a real defensive rebound in right. He names the red flag himself: a 10-point hard-hit drop. The case holds up, and it makes letting Suzuki walk for a comp pick look worse.

articles.author: Evan Altman
articles.take: Altman frames Bart as the Kelly replacement and argues Kelly was a journeyman too before his Cubs run. Fair point on Kelly's history, but it dodges the gap: Kelly just put up 1.9 bWAR and Bart put up 0.3. Cheap is not the same as equivalent.
articles.title: Cubs Claim Catcher Joey Bart off Waivers from White Sox

articles.author: Matthew Trueblood
articles.take: Called the roster-math logic exactly: Roberts and Arias out, Steele kept because the Cubs can't afford to lose an arm they can't count on. The note that eight out-of-options relievers clog the 40-man is the sharpest point anyone made this week.
articles.title: 4 Chicago Cubs Non-Tender Candidates on Deadline Day

articles.author: Staff
articles.take: Mostly hitting coach Dustin Kelly talking up Busch's 'in between' version and a healthy Shaw. It's useful as a read on the internal-options plan, but it never presses on the obvious question: who replaces Suzuki's right-handed power. Club-voice piece with little pushback.
articles.title: While Chicago Cubs need to reinforce rotation, they can't ignore addressing the offense in offseason plans

articles.author: Casey Drottar
articles.take: Good reporting on the blister problem and Hoyer owning the Cabrera miss. The piece treats 'get more out of him' as a rotation plan, and it isn't one. It's the best explanation yet of why the Cubs keep talking about the arms they have instead of buying new ones.
articles.title: Cubs' goal for Cabrera is clear: 'We have to get more out of him'

articles.author: Matthew Trueblood
articles.take: Confirms the interest with his own source, then argues the Cubs have to take one big risk this winter and Duran is the cheapest version. The tools case from 2024 is real. But he lists Sato, Taira and Rogers as the other risks and never squares that the Cubs can't afford to spend a risk on a bat while the rotation is empty. The clubhouse-and-fans section is the most honest part of any Duran piece so far.
articles.title: Is Jarren Duran the Right Kind of Problem for Cubs to Try to Solve?

column.title: Everyone is waiting on Skubal. The Cubs can't afford to.
column.dek: The Mets put nearly $400 million on the table, Morosi says King and Peralta won't sign until Skubal does, and the Cubs just lost control of their own calendar.

p: Jim Duquette reported Friday that the Mets have offered Tarik Skubal nine years and almost $400 million. Skubal is expected to choose by Dec. 1. That alone isn't a Cubs story; they told everyone back on Nov. 9, through Sahadev Sharma, that they weren't getting into the bidding.

The Cubs story is the next sentence. Jon Paul Morosi said on MLB Network Friday that Michael King and Freddy Peralta, the two best starters on the market after Skubal, probably won't sign until Skubal does. Those are the two names at the top of the Cubs' own list. So the front office that chose to stay out of the Skubal race has tied its whole winter to the Skubal race anyway.

Think about who comes out of the Skubal sweepstakes empty-handed. At least three of the Mets, Blue Jays, Dodgers and Padres will lose. Every one of them has a rotation hole and money budgeted for an ace. The minute Skubal signs, those clubs turn to King and Peralta with that money already set aside.

Peralta already has more than six suitors, per Jim Bowden: the Padres, the Rays, maybe the Braves, and the White Sox, who just cleared $25.15 million by moving Luis Castillo. Morosi has the White Sox on King too. If Skubal picks on Nov. 29, the Cubs get 48 hours to outbid the deepest pockets in baseball for the No. 2 tier. That isn't a plan. It's a hope.

There is one part of this market that doesn't care about Skubal. The NPB posting windows close on their own clock, and Hiromi Itoh, Kaima Taira and Teruaki Sato all have to sign by Dec. 1 whatever happens in Orange County.

Itoh was in Chicago Friday, per ESPN's Jorge Castillo. He threw 172 2/3 innings of 3.18 ERA ball in 2026 with 159 strikeouts and 34 walks, and MLBTR projects two years and $20 million. That's a No. 5 starter at a No. 5 price, and the Cubs can close it this week without waiting on anyone. Taira is a four-team fight with the Mets now in. Both should be getting offers now, not after Skubal signs.

body.h: Tender day told you the plan
p: Friday's moves were Joey Bart off waivers and Braxton Roxby for cash. Thursday was Chayce McDermott, a 28-year-old with a 10.18 career ERA. The 40-man sits at 37. Zero starters have been added, and every pitcher who finished 2026 in the rotation is gone.

The money isn't the excuse. The Cubs ran a club-record $265.6 million tax payroll in 2026. MLBTR projects 2027 at about $169 million, and Cubbies Crib puts the room under the tax line near $68 million. Close to $100 million came off the books. Not spending it before the lockout is a choice, and it's the same choice that sent five arms out the door without a counteroffer.

Mike Petriello's piece Saturday on MLB.com is the cleanest case yet for what the Cubs are letting go. Over the last four years, Seiya Suzuki and Randy Arozarena have the same line: 14 fWAR, about 30% better than league average at the plate, a 25% strikeout rate and an 11% walk rate. Petriello leans Suzuki on the stuff that ages: 63rd-percentile bat speed against Arozarena's 31st, an 89th-percentile chase rate, and a +7 fielding run value year in right that made him a Gold Glove finalist.

He's honest about the flaw. Suzuki's hard-hit rate fell 10 points, one of the five biggest drops in baseball, because his squared-up rate fell apart. That's real. It's also not enough to explain walking away from a 131 OPS+ bat for a pick after the fourth round. If the Cubs aren't paying Suzuki four years and $105 million, fine. That money has one job, and the deadline is Dec. 1.

Stop waiting for the market to sort itself out. Put Peralta in front of a real number now: four years at a premium AAV with an expiration date. Make him decide before Skubal does, while the Cubs are bidding against six teams instead of nine. Sign Itoh this week. Keep pressing on Taira.

If the Cubs reach the lockout with Cabrera, Steele and Assad as three-fifths of the rotation, the 2027 season is decided in November. They don't get to blame the market for that. They're the ones who decided to wait on it.

items.name: Pete Crow-Armstrong
items.note: Unanimous NL MVP. 45 HR, 41 SB, NL-best .942 OPS, MLB-best 10.6 fWAR. Hank Aaron Award, All-MLB First Team, Platinum Glove.

items.name: Seiya Suzuki
items.note: 131 OPS+, career-best 5.1 bWAR, Gold Glove finalist.

items.name: Alex Bregman
items.note: 5.8 bWAR, NL Gold Glove at third, All-MLB Second Team, ninth in MVP voting. Hitless in October.

items.name: Michael Conforto
items.note: 118 OPS+ on a minor-league deal.

items.name: Carson Kelly
items.note: 97 OPS+ and 1.9 bWAR from a catcher is a win.

items.name: Michael Busch
items.note: 106 OPS+ at first base. The walks carried him.

items.name: Ian Happ
items.note: 103 OPS+, 189 strikeouts, platooned by September.

items.name: Miguel Amaya
items.note: 98 OPS+, propped up by a .315 BABIP.

items.name: Pedro Ramírez
items.note: Held short together at 22. The xwOBA says he was lucky.

items.name: Nico Hoerner
items.note: 84 OPS+. The xBA says he deserved better; the glove is elite.

items.name: Matt Shaw
items.note: 102 OPS+ with a .303 xwOBA. Still looking for a position.

items.name: Dansby Swanson
items.note: His worst year as a Cub at the plate (90 OPS+). The glove saved the grade.

items.name: Ben Brown
items.note: 228 ERA+ over 68 innings before the neck gave out. Neck surgery Nov. 9; back around midseason.

items.name: David Peterson
items.note: 114 ERA+ after the June trade.

items.name: Shota Imanaga
items.note: 32 starts and a 112 ERA+. The 35 homers keep it from an A.

items.name: Matthew Boyd
items.note: 108 ERA+ in 22 starts, then two first-inning homers in Game 1.

items.name: Javier Assad
items.note: 3.63 ERA, 4.92 FIP. The defense did him favors.

items.name: Ryan Rolison
items.note: 135 ERA+ in middle relief from a waiver claim.

items.name: Colin Rea
items.note: 137 innings at a 97 ERA+. Exactly what he is.

items.name: Jacob Webb
items.note: Nine saves, eight blown.

items.name: Kevin Gausman
items.note: 4.83 ERA and 0.1 bWAR after the deadline deal.

items.name: Clay Holmes
items.note: 1.55 ERA over his first five starts, 8.24 over his last four.

items.name: Edward Cabrera
items.note: 71 ERA+, -1.4 bWAR, left off the Wild Card roster.

items.name: Jameson Taillon
items.note: 25 homers in 76 innings, -0.9 bWAR.

items.name: The bullpen
items.note: 28 blown saves, a third of inherited runners scored, 14 different save-getters.

items.name: Crow-Armstrong extension (6 yr, $115M)
items.note: The reigning unanimous MVP at about $19M a year through 2032. The best contract in baseball.

items.name: Bregman signing (5 yr, $175M)
items.note: 5.8 bWAR in year one. Years four and five are the risk.

items.name: Conforto minor-league deal
items.note: 118 OPS+ for almost nothing.

items.name: Peterson trade
items.note: 114 ERA+ in 15 starts.

items.name: Hoerner extension (6 yr, $141M)
items.note: Paying a glove-first second baseman through his age-35 season.

items.name: Gausman trade
items.note: A deadline splash worth 0.1 bWAR.

items.name: Cabrera trade (Caissie + 2)
items.note: The No. 1 prospect for 80 innings of 5.96 ERA.

items.name: Holmes trade (Rojas)
items.note: A top-two prospect for nine starts, zero postseason innings, and he opted out.

items.name: Bullpen construction
items.note: Hoyer's own words: 'I did a poor job on the bullpen this year, full stop.'

items.name: Kelly option declined ($1.5M buyout)
items.note: The right call on a mutual option. It only stays a B if they re-sign him or find a real starter.

items.name: Suzuki qualifying offer
items.note: Paid off as planned: he rejected it Tuesday, so the Cubs get a pick after the fourth round when he signs elsewhere.

items.name: No QO for Happ
items.note: He'd likely have taken $23.15M. Saying no was the disciplined call.

items.name: No QO for Boyd
items.note: A 36-year-old No. 5 isn't worth the risk of an acceptance.

items.name: Rea, Harvey, Thielbar options declined
items.note: $2.5M in buyouts to clear three arms that didn't miss bats or didn't pitch.

items.name: Assad option declined ($3.3M)
items.note: Saves about $1M through arbitration and keeps a useful swingman. Small, correct, and an honest read of a 4.92 FIP.

items.name: Webb restructure
items.note: Same $2.5M guarantee and a 2028 option. Smart, small.

items.name: Orze waiver claim
items.note: A 5.66 ERA with no options left. A free look, nothing more.

items.name: Sitting out Skubal (per Sharma)
items.note: $97M came off the books and the answer is 'we can't match the Dodgers.' It becomes a C only if King or Peralta and a trade arm land before Dec. 1.

items.name: Internal plan for LF, RF and C (per Hawkins)
items.note: Hawkins admits the risk: unproven corners to pay for 'proven guys in other spots.' Fine as a trade-off. It stays a C- until those proven guys exist.

items.name: Kanzler replaced (Ben Martin, farm director)
items.note: Fast, internal and sensible. Adding Rylan Domingues on the pitching-analytics side is the right department.

items.name: Wiggins, McCullough added to the 40-man
items.note: Protects the Detmers trade chip and a Double-A arm with a 27.7% K rate. Correct and routine.

items.name: This offseason so far
items.note: Option calls and QOs mostly right, zero starters added, a public pass on Skubal. May and Gray signed elsewhere, Seattle sold its spare starters to Kansas City, and Loaisiga went back to the Yankees. Tender day brought Joey Bart and Braxton Roxby. Eleven days to the lockout.

items.name: Holmes reunion interest (per Hawkins)
items.note: They traded a top prospect for nine starts, he opted out, and the GM wants him back at a projected three years. Only a one-year swingman deal gets this off a D.

items.name: Justin Lawrence (likely minor-league deal)
items.note: Free Triple-A depth with a 5.34 career ERA and a walk problem. Harmless, and not the impact arm.

items.name: Missing the Mariners' starter sale
items.note: Seattle wanted a third baseman and a right-handed bat, the Cubs had both to spare, and Kansas City got Miller and Evans. Dipoto now says 'zero' more.

items.name: McDermott waiver claim
items.note: Free, uses an empty roster spot, 30.5% minor-league K rate. Also a 14.6% walk rate and no options. Depth, not help.

items.name: Bart waiver claim
items.note: An 82 OPS+ backup for about $3M is fine. As the Kelly replacement it's a D.

items.name: Roxby for cash
items.note: Optionable arm with a 94.6 mph heater for nothing. Smarter than another out-of-options claim.

items.name: Arias, Roberts non-tendered
items.note: Correct roster math. Leaves the backup infield thin.

regressionNotes.663423: A 15.8% K rate. That ERA belonged to the defense.
regressionNotes.663538: The one regular who was unlucky. A .296 xBA says the average comes back.
regressionNotes.664023: Small gap. The .218 is mostly him.
regressionNotes.665795: xFIP says unlucky; an 8th-percentile xERA says hitters crushed him. Don't bank on a big bounce.
regressionNotes.665804: A .315 BABIP for a catcher. Expect the OBP to slip.
regressionNotes.669020: Middle-relief ERA, back-end peripherals. Fine in low leverage.
regressionNotes.673548: The expected line is still well above average. Price him on that, not the surface numbers.
regressionNotes.676962: Still very good, just not 228-ERA+ good.
regressionNotes.691718: Even after the haircut, a .372 xwOBA is elite.
regressionNotes.699393: The largest gap on the team. Don't pencil him into a corner spot off this line.
